additionalCfgTestScope: The new lib.rs and sherlock/mod.rs declare additional cfg(test) modules. Their source bytes are pinned in this report, but no test membership adoption or execution is inferred.

linePointers.text: pub fn compile_selected(source: &str, selector: &RelationSelector) -> Result<SelectedRelation, DriverError> {

sourceFacts.sourceFact: Public Sherlock plus two source adapter modules are declared; draft parser/typechecker/bridge modules are cfg(test).
Ordinary Sherlock module declarations and exports name compare/reference/reference_stream/reference_display/reference_types.
Additional draft/helper/image/layout/arithmetic modules are under cfg(test) in this entry point.
Source projection reports false function/branch/recursion/data support and evaluation_performed false.
Projection explicitly checks /1 profile; excludes state/asset declarations; admits ordered lets and a final emit value.
Projection maps a restricted scalar operator set and reports liabilities or effect statements as unsupported projection metadata.
New public source describes a bounded host observation consumer, not a new compiler/profile; source H1 qualification is retained.
Host observation entry takes explicit caller bounds and invokes Core validation; source code only was inspected.
run_steps groups existing step records and stops on terminal publication.
visit_steps adds callback observation grouping, with Budget/Terminal/Observer stop metadata.
Draft parser declares moriarty-sherlock-draft/1, distinct from moriarty/1.
Draft grammar reads program/functions/entry into the Sherlock AST; lib.rs gates this module under cfg(test).
Backend adds public sherlock_machine and source_projection module exports.
compile_reported dispatches to existing compile_signed or compile, then constructs a separate source-static projection report.
Main compile command consumes compile_reported and publishes source-projection.json before publish_artifact.
Core language and semantics constants remain moriarty/1 and moriarty-core/1 in byte-identical ir.rs.

conclusions: This is not a doc-only upstream change: new public source adapters, host observation APIs, backend source modules and a CLI sidecar consumer are present.

Within the frozen70 membership, only lib.rs differs; the parser, Core IR, runtime including financial-duty code, stage admission/IR and related files are full-byte equal to new upstream. Byte equality alone does not establish semantic compatibility.
The frozen70 membership does not contain the eight Sherlock files directly required by the new ordinary Core module declarations. Simply replacing lib.rs does not reconcile that source membership.

The main CLI now goes through compile_reported and writes source-projection.json. The delivered mori-k2 source instead still calls mori_r1cs::compile_source via its frozen frontend; no sidecar or new language support is inferred for it.
Draft functions/branches/lists/trees use moriarty-sherlock-draft/1 and cfg(test) source; they are not newly registered /1 or staged /2 admissions.
No Source/5 or Source/6 legacy profile is relabelled as current Rust; no backend lowering, proof, correspondence or ledger qualification is established.
securityQuestionsForOpus: Interpretation/admission of the new public host observation entry and its H1 qualifications.
Security/circuit meaning of new mori-backend sherlock_machine source constructors and any required binding/refusal obligations.
Security-sensitive source/build identity policy for an enlarged Core membership; this report only identifies the missing named source dependencies.
